messages.subject: Filter other loc.metrics 2
parts:
Hi,

I have set up an earlier question about filtering AvgCountRef and hence the title. I tried to reuse my old script but it doesn't seem to work properly anymore.

Here is what I tried to do

> gl6 <- gl3[,gl3@other$loc.metrics$CombCount >= 5]
> gl6 <- gl6[,gl6@other$loc.metrics$CombCount <= 500]
> min(gl6@other$loc.metrics$CombCount)
[1] 4.214286
> max(gl6@other$loc.metrics$CombCount)
[1] 1509.698
________________________________________________________________________________

I also tried this:
> read.depth <- data.frame(cbind(g...@loc.names, gl3@other$loc.metrics$CombCount)) > read.depth[,2] <- as.numeric(read.depth[,2])
> read.depth.filter <- filter(read.depth, read.depth[,2] >= 5 & read.depth[,2] <= 500)
> min(read.depth.filter[,2])
[1] 5
> max(read.depth.filter[,2])
[1] 500
> depth.filter.loci <- read.depth.filter[,1]
> gl5 <- gl.keep.loc(gl3, loc.list = depth.filter.loci)
> min(gl5@other$loc.metrics$CombCount)
[1] 10.04671
> max(gl5@other$loc.metrics$CombCount)
[1] 127.9611

I still haven't got the correct numbers. Am I missing something or is there a different way to do this? Any help with this would be much appreciated.

Thanks,
Rujiporn

Hi Rujiporn,

I could not find a field named CombCount. Could you please be more specific about what you want to filter.

> read.depth <- gl.filter.rdepth(gl3, lower = 5, upper = 500, verbose = NULL)

Regards,
Luis

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Filter other loc.metrics 2
parts:
Hi Rujiporn:

I think the problem is the way you are subsetting your data. The genlight object and the data stored in @other are not linked, so when you subset your genlight object based on a metric stored in @other$loc.metrics "by hand" it doesn't subset automatically the data stored in @other. The correct way to do it by hand is:
 
 gl3 <- gl_test
 # number of loci before filtering
 nLoc(gl3)
 # [1] 1000

 # adding dummy data
 gl3@other$loc.metrics$test <- 1:nLoc(gl3)
 min(gl3@other$loc.metrics$test)
 # [1] 1
 max(gl3@other$loc.metrics$test)
 # [1] 1000
 
 gl6 <- gl3[ ,which(gl3@other$loc.metrics$test >= 5 & gl3@other$loc.metrics$test <= 500)]
# updating @other$loc.metrics. Loci are in the rows, so the comma goes at the end
 gl6@other$loc.metrics <-  gl3@other$loc.metrics[which(gl3@other$loc.metrics$test >= 5 & gl6@other$loc.metrics$test <= 500),]
 
# number of loci after filtering
 nLoc(gl6)
 # [1] 496
 
 min(gl6@other$loc.metrics$test)
 # [1] 5
 max(gl6@other$loc.metrics$test)
 # [1] 500
 
The above process, and other updates on the data, are integrated in the filters functions of dartR.

Regarding the read depth issue: read depth is calculated in the dartR function gl.read.dart as follows:

        for (i in 1:nLoc(glout)) {
            called.ind <- round(nInd(glout) * glout@other$loc.metrics$CallRate[i],
                0)
            ref.count <- called.ind * glout@other$loc.metrics$OneRatioRef[i]
            alt.count <- called.ind * glout@other$loc.metrics$OneRatioSnp[i]
            sum.count.ref <- ref.count * glout@other$loc.metrics$AvgCountRef[i]
            sum.count.alt <- alt.count * glout@other$loc.metrics$AvgCountSnp[i]
            glout@other$loc.metrics$rdepth[i] <- round((sum.count.alt +
                sum.count.ref)/called.ind, 1)
        }
    }
        
# The metrics used to calculate read depth are the following which are reported by DART:
# CallRate        The proportion of samples for which the genotype call is either "1" or "0", rather than "-"
# OneRatioRef        The proportion of samples for which the genotype score is "1", in the Reference allele row   
# OneRatioSnp        The proportion of samples for which the genotype score is "1", in the SNP allele row   
# AvgCountRef        The sum of the tag read counts for all samples, divided by the number of samples with non-zero tag read counts, for the Reference allele row
# AvgCountSnp        The sum of the tag read counts for all samples, divided by the number of samples with non-zero tag read counts, for the SNP allele row

Please let me know if this what you were looking for, otherwise I am happy to help further.

Cheers,
Luis
